bounded_slice.leaf: evidence-package durability across GitHub repository-network lifecycle changes
bounded_slice.method: First-party GitHub documentation only; no destructive experiment and no second leaf.
bounded_slice.tested_scope: Whether a commit-SHA plus GitHub verification evidence package remains replayable when a fork/upstream is deleted, repository visibility changes, or a fork leaves its network. Branch-deletion-only reachability was not independently resolved in this slice.

observations.observation: Deleting a public repository does not delete its public forks, while deleting a private repository deletes its forks; some deleted repositories may be restorable for a limited period.

For a public upstream deletion, an active public fork becomes the new upstream. GitHub also states that commits from a deleted fork can remain accessible to the repository network. Visibility changes can split repositories into different networks.

Persistent commit-signature verification records are stored by GitHub and are explicitly scoped to the repository network; the record is reused when the same commit appears in the same repository or its forks.
Leaving a fork network preserves Git commit metadata but permanently disconnects the repository from the prior network and discards multiple GitHub-side metadata classes.

inferences: A narrow replay path survives public-upstream deletion when an active public fork keeps the repository network alive; this is not equivalent to deletion-independent durability.

The verification-record guarantee is network-scoped, so the first-party documentation does not justify claiming that the same GitHub verification record follows a commit across a network split or detach.

A package that depends only on GitHub-hosted repository-network persistence cannot satisfy the stronger all-lifecycle durability claim: private repository deletion removes its private forks, and the docs provide no zero-external-backup guarantee that the commit plus verification record remains replayable after the whole relevant network becomes inaccessible.

Therefore the tested mechanism is a partial pass for surviving same-network cases and a fail for network-independent durability. The unresolved child is branch/object reachability and verification behavior after ordinary branch deletion or a network split, without introducing backup services or manual restoration.
uncertainty: No destructive deletion/visibility-change experiment was executed.
The cited docs do not establish indefinite object retention after all references and the relevant network disappear.
The cited detachment documentation guarantees Git commit metadata preservation, not transfer of GitHub's network-scoped persistent verification record.

hard_gates.conflict_check: No O/O-derived, downstream, other-worker semantic input, shared ledger, or scheduler mutation was used. Repository APIs were transport only; public evidence was first-party GitHub documentation.

continuation: Next invocation re-bootstrap/freeze authority and reconstruct p1-sa-604.
